title: Hom sheaves out of a finitely presented constant sheaf
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a discrete commutative ring and $X$ a scheme. For a
$\Lambda$-module $M$ write $\underline M=\nu_X^*M_{X,\Et}$ for its constant sheaf
on $X_{\Proet}$, where $M_{X,\Et}$ is the constant étale sheaf. Let
$\Lambda^m\xrightarrow{a}\Lambda^n\to M\to0$ be a finite presentation.

1. For every $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf $N$ on $X_{\Proet}$ there is a natural
   isomorphism $\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_X}(\underline M,N)\cong
   \ker\bigl(a^{\mathsf T}\colon N^n\to N^m\bigr)$.
2. For $M,M'$ finitely presented,
   $\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_X}(\underline M,\underline{M'})\cong
   \underline{\Hom_\Lambda(M,M')}$, compatibly with composition.
3. $\mathcal Aut_{\Lambda_X}(\underline M)\cong\nu_X^*\bigl(\operatorname{Aut}_\Lambda(M)_{X,\Et}\bigr)$
   as sheaves of groups; in particular it is a classical sheaf of groups.

proof.text: Write $C_\Et(E)=E_{X,\Et}$ and $C(E)=\nu_X^*C_\Et(E)$, for sets as well as modules, and put $\Lambda_X=C(\Lambda)$. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $C_\Et$ is sheafification of the constant presheaf. Constant presheaves preserve finite limits and exact sequences because these are computed at each object. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], sheafifying a constant $\Lambda$-module presheaf gives a module over the sheafified constant ring, with underlying abelian sheaf its abelian sheafification. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] give exactness and finite-limit preservation of $C_\Et$ on modules. The module functor $\nu_X^*$ is exact for every discrete commutative $\Lambda$ by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], not only for finite rings. Consequently $C$ is exact, preserves finite products and kernels on modules, and $C(\Lambda^r)=\Lambda_X^r$ for every finite $r$. For sets, [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] and the finite-limit-preserving comparison inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] show that $C$ preserves finite limits. These set and module constructions agree on underlying sets: this is [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] for $C_\Et$, followed by applying the comparison inverse image to the addition and action maps. All diagrams and the chosen site skeletons are small in the larger universe fixed for these sites.

source.place: opening paragraph; exactness supplied by Stacks 03CY, 00WJ, 03DA and 03DB

proof.text: Let $b:\Lambda^n\to M$ be the presentation quotient. Step 1 gives the exact presentation $\Lambda_X^m\xrightarrow{C(a)}\Lambda_X^n\xrightarrow{C(b)}C(M)\to0$. Fix any object $V$ of $X_{\Proet}$ and use the localized site and sectionwise restriction of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The abelian restriction functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact]; apply this to the two short exact sequences through the image of $C(a)$ to preserve the displayed presentation. The forgetful descriptions in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] give the same assertion for $\Lambda_X|_V$-modules. Write $\Lambda_V=\Lambda_X|_V$. For every finite $r$, a map $\Lambda_V^r\to N|_V$ is determined by its values $x_i\in N(V)$ on the basis sections at the terminal object $V/V$. Conversely $(x_i)$ gives, at each $W\to V$, the linear map $(t_i)\mapsto\sum_i t_i(x_i|_W)$. These formulas are inverse and commute with restriction and with maps of $N$.

source.place: paragraph (1): the restricted presentation and the free-module Hom calculation

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel], the quotient $C(b)|_V$ of step 2 is a cokernel of $C(a)|_V$. Hence maps $C(M)|_V\to N|_V$ correspond bijectively to maps $\Lambda_V^n\to N|_V$ annihilating $C(a)|_V$. If $a(e_k)=\sum_i a_{ik}e_i$, the tuple $(x_i)$ of step 2 annihilates this map precisely when $\sum_i a_{ik}x_i=0$ for every $k$, namely $a^{\mathsf T}(x)=0$. The bijection sends $\varphi$ to $(\varphi(C(b)(e_i)))_i$; its inverse is the unique cokernel factorization of the basis-value map. Uniqueness shows that both bijections commute with $V'\to V$ and with every coefficient map $N\to N'$. The defining sections of [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and the sectionwise kernels of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] therefore identify these bijections with the natural isomorphism in (1). This uses the sheaf cokernel universal property, and does not assume that $N(V)$ is an exact functor of $N$.

source.place: paragraph (1): explicit cokernel factorization and transpose coefficients

proof.text: For modules $P,Q$ put $H_{P,Q}=\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(P,Q)$. Apply the set functor $C$ of step 1 to evaluation $H_{P,Q}\times P\to Q$ and use its finite-product comparison. This gives $e_{P,Q}:C(H_{P,Q})\times C(P)\to C(Q)$. The module identities $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ and $f(\lambda x)=\lambda f(x)$ are equalities of maps on finite products of the sets $H_{P,Q},P,\Lambda$; applying $C$ proves that evaluation at a local section of $C(H_{P,Q})$ is a $\Lambda_X$-linear map on the corresponding slice site. The identities $(f+g)(x)=f(x)+g(x)$ and $(\lambda f)(x)=\lambda f(x)$ likewise show linearity in the parameter. By the sectionwise definition of [def-pur-sheaf-hom] we obtain a canonical linear map $c_{P,Q}:C(H_{P,Q})\to\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_X}(C(P),C(Q))$. Restriction commutes with these maps since $e_{P,Q}$ is a sheaf map. A constant parameter $f$ gives exactly $C(f)$: apply $C$ to the equality $\operatorname{ev}(f,-)=f$.

source.place: paragraph (2): the canonical comparison is defined by evaluation, with its linearity equations

proof.text: Take $P=M,Q=M'$. For any $\Lambda$-module $Q$, the ordinary presentation gives $H_{M,Q}=\ker(Q^n\to Q^m)$: a tuple $(y_i)$ defines the map $\Lambda^n\to Q$, $(t_i)\mapsto\sum_i t_i y_i$, and it descends uniquely to $M$ if and only if all $\sum_i a_{ik}y_i$ vanish. Step 1 and the sectionwise module kernels of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] therefore give $C(H_{M,M'})\cong\ker(C(M')^n\to C(M')^m)$. Under the basis-value identification in (1), the map $c_{M,M'}$ of step 4 is this comparison: its $i$th coordinate is $C(f\mapsto f(b(e_i)))$, by evaluation. Both maps to $C(M')^n$ thus agree coordinate by coordinate. It follows that $c_{M,M'}$ is an isomorphism; its inverse is the isomorphism in (2). Only finite presentation of the source $M$ is used in this calculation; the stated finite presentation of $M'$ is certainly sufficient.

source.place: paragraph (2): finite kernel comparison, with the actual comparison map identified

proof.text: For modules $P,Q,R$, the equality $\operatorname{ev}_{P,R}(g\circ f,x)=\operatorname{ev}_{Q,R}(g,\operatorname{ev}_{P,Q}(f,x))$ is an equality of maps $H_{Q,R}\times H_{P,Q}\times P\to R$. Applying the product-preserving set functor $C$ proves that the maps $c_{P,Q}$ of step 4 intertwine composition of module homomorphisms and composition of sheaf homomorphisms. Indeed, at every $V$, the two resulting linear maps on $C(P)|_V$ have equal evaluations on every further object $W\to V$, hence are identical by [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Applying $C$ to $\operatorname{ev}_{P,P}(1,x)=x$ proves preservation of identity as well. Restricting to finitely presented modules, the isomorphisms of step 5 and their inverses consequently respect composition and identity. No assertion that all global sections of a constant sheaf are constant is needed.

source.place: paragraph (2), final sentence: explicit composition and identity equations

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)$ as a set with composition. Define $I\subset E\times E$ by $I=\{(f,g):f\circ g=1,\ g\circ f=1\}$. It is the equalizer of $(f,g)\mapsto(f\circ g,g\circ f)$ and the constant map $(f,g)\mapsto(1,1)$ into $E\times E$. By the sectionwise limit description of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], the identical equalizer for $\mathcal End(C(M))$ has sections pairs of mutually inverse sheaf endomorphisms on each slice. Projection to the first factor identifies it with $\mathcal Aut(C(M))$: its inverse sends an automorphism $u$ to $(u,u^{-1})$, and uniqueness of inverse makes this commute with restriction. Steps 1, 5 and 6 identify this equalizer with $C(I)$. The elementary bijection $I\to\operatorname{Aut}_\Lambda(M)$, $(f,g)\mapsto f$, has inverse $f\mapsto(f,f^{-1})$. The group operation on pairs is $(f,g)(h,k)=(f\circ h,k\circ g)$, so the composition compatibility of step 6 identifies the resulting isomorphism $\mathcal Aut(C(M))\cong C(\operatorname{Aut}_\Lambda(M))$ with an isomorphism of sheaves of groups. We use finite limits of SETS here: composition and the invertibility locus are not linear maps or submodules.

source.place: paragraph (3): inverse pairs as a finite limit of sets, including the group operation

proof.text: By definition of $C$ on sets, the last sheaf of step 7 is $\nu_X^*(\operatorname{Aut}_\Lambda(M)_{X,\Et})$. Apply [det-pe-classical-sheaves-image] to its underlying sheaf of sets: condition (1) holds with the constant étale sheaf $\operatorname{Aut}_\Lambda(M)_{X,\Et}$, so condition (2) gives classicality. This is precisely classicality of the underlying sheaf of the group in (3); the group structure has already been identified in step 7.

source.place: paragraph (3), last sentence: essential-image criterion on sets
